QF.id: Terminology in Equity and Debt Markets_16

question.text: Credit rating agencies in India include:

answer.text: CRISIL, ICRA, CARE, and India Ratings

explanation.text: The Logic: In Indian capital markets, SEBI-registered credit rating agencies (CRAs) assess the creditworthiness of debt issuers and instruments. Among the well-known SEBI-registered CRAs operating in India are CRISIL, ICRA, CARE Ratings, and India Ratings & Research (an affiliate of Fitch). They assign credit ratings used by investors to gauge default risk. The Trap: Option A names regulators (RBI, SEBI, IRDAI), not raters. Option C names stock exchanges (NSE, BSE, MSEI), which match buyers and sellers rather than rate credit. Option D names depositories (NSDL, CDSL), which hold securities in dematerialised form. Note: The cited NISM-Series-XV Research Analyst workbook discusses credit rating agencies and credit risk generally, but the explicit list 'CRISIL, ICRA, CARE, and India Ratings' was not located in the pages reviewed. The agency-name list above reflects publicly known SEBI-registered CRAs rather than a direct workbook citation.
